content:
More than a year ago, Jony Ive and Sam Altman previewed an entirely new concept in AI hardware, making major promises at the time.

The latest reporting suggests that OpenAI may technically be able to deliver on those promises, but the end result could end up competing with an upcoming AirPods model. If that turns out to be the case, I can easily imagine AirPods Ultra being the more popular choice…

The promise of an OpenAI hardware device

In a video the two of them published last May, they previewed this AI hardware device. The video was disappointingly light on the exact form the device would take, but they did claim it would be something entirely new that no one had ever seen before.

"I think this is going to be the coolest piece of technology that the world will have ever seen." "So we at least should think that there are other possibilities, beyond these traditional products." "I am absolutely certain that we are on the verge of a new generation of technology that can make us all better versions of ourselves."

As I said at the time, anyone making those kinds of promises should not end up producing a product form factor we've already seen.

A smart speaker with built-in camera and sensors

A smart speaker is certainly one smart hardware product we've seen before. However, the latest reporting suggests that this is exactly what we should now expect. Bloomberg says what will set it apart will be the addition of a camera and other sensors.

Whether that can truly be called a whole new category of technology is debatable, but it's not hard to see how such a device would be considerably more powerful than existing smart speakers.

But it could end up competing with AirPods Ultra

However, this combination of a device you can talk to plus a camera that can sense its surroundings isn't exactly new. Our iPhones can already do this via Visual Intelligence, and we've seen it in Meta's smart glasses and other competitors. In the end, it sounds just like what we're expecting from the upcoming AirPods Ultra.

Of course, a speaker and earbuds wouldn't compete directly, but the use cases do overlap. A smart speaker is more convenient at home—no need to put anything in your ears—and multiple people can use it at once. But OpenAI specifically talked about a device you could carry around with you, and I have to admit that for use outside the home, the AirPods form factor is clearly far more convenient.

Maybe we'll be surprised in the end, but as things stand, I find it hard to imagine myself regularly carrying around a portable speaker, except in situations where I would already be doing so—like going away for the weekend and wanting to listen to good music in a hotel room or vacation rental. Unlike what the promo video hinted at, I really can't imagine a scenario in which I'd bring it to a bar.

For me, AirPods Ultra seems to have significantly more potential than a smarter speaker. What do you think? Please take part in our poll and share your views in the comments section.
